stem: A client asks why a serum total-protein test was ordered. Which explanation is most appropriate?

options.A: It identifies a single disease from the protein value itself, so other laboratory findings and clinical assessment are generally unnecessary.
options.B: It directly measures glomerular filtration and is primarily used as a stand-alone estimate of kidney filtration efficiency.
options.C: It helps evaluate abnormal protein states related to plasma-water changes or altered protein concentrations, but interpretation requires clinical context.
options.D: It measures stored iron in circulating red cells and is primarily used to establish iron-deficiency anemia without other testing.

rationale: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories guidance states that serum total protein is useful in evaluating a variety of liver, kidney, bone-marrow, metabolic, and nutritional disorders. Mayo explains that the two broad causes of altered serum total protein are changes in plasma-water volume and changes in the concentration of one or more plasma proteins. Hyperproteinemia may occur with dehydration or increased polyclonal/monoclonal protein production, while hypoproteinemia can occur with hemodilution or low albumin. Therefore C is correct. The test is not disease-specific, does not directly measure GFR, and does not measure iron stores.
educational_objective: Recognize serum total protein as a nonspecific laboratory measure that helps evaluate abnormal protein states and requires correlation with the clinical context and other findings.
source_version_date: Current online Test Catalog; test definition generated May 13, 2026; live page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Useful For: evaluation of diseases involving liver, kidney, bone marrow, metabolic or nutritional disorders. Clinical Information: altered total protein reflects changes in plasma-water volume or concentrations of specific plasma proteins; dehydration, inflammatory polyclonal production, and monoclonal production can raise total protein.
source_claim_supported: Serum total protein is a nonspecific measure affected by hydration and protein concentrations/production and must be interpreted in clinical context.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — laboratory-test interpretation.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths and retained serum total protein as a broad, nonspecific laboratory measure rather than a stand-alone diagnosis.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — Mayo directly identifies hydration and protein-concentration mechanisms and broad diagnostic use; C is the only appropriately qualified interpretation.
